---
title: The protocol layer
---

`alpha_led_sign.protocol` is the Alpha protocol with no I/O: Commands in, bytes out,
and bytes in, Responses out. `Sign` is built on it. You need it to send a Command
that has no `Sign` method, to nest several Commands in one Packet, or to see the
bytes the library sends.

## Send any Command

Every Command is a class in `alpha_led_sign.protocol`. `Sign.send` checks Commands
against the Sign Model and sends them in one Packet:

```python
from alpha_led_sign.protocol import ClearSerialErrorStatus, WriteString

sign.send(ClearSerialErrorStatus(), WriteString("T", "72F"))
print(sign.serial_errors().ok)    # did that Packet arrive intact?
```

A Packet with more than one Command is **nested**. The Sign needs 100 ms of
silence after each Command's start in a nested Packet, which the library keeps.
Reads, tones, and Clear Memory must be the last Command in a Packet.

`Sign.query` sends one read and returns its parsed answer:

```python
from alpha_led_sign.protocol import ReadDayOfWeek

sign.query(ReadDayOfWeek())    # Weekday.SUNDAY
```

## See the bytes

`encode_packet` turns Commands into a `Packet`. `bytes(packet)` gives the whole
Packet, which is useful for logging and tests:

```python
from alpha_led_sign.protocol import Frame, Message, Recipient, WriteText, encode_packet

hello = WriteText("A", Message(Frame(None, content="HELLO")))
packet = encode_packet(Recipient("Z", 0), [hello])
bytes(packet)
# b'\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01Z00\x02AAHELLO\x0301FB\x04'
```

That is the worked example from Appendix F of the manual. A `Packet` is a tuple of
`Chunk`s, each with the seconds of silence that must follow it.

## Write a Transport

A Transport is any object with four methods: `write`, `pause`, `read`, and
`close`. `SerialTransport` is the one the library ships. Write another to reach a
Sign some other way, or to record what the library sends:

```python
class Recorder:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.sent: list[bytes] = []

    def write(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        self.sent.append(data)

    def pause(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        pass

    def read(self, timeout: float) -> bytes:
        return b""

    def close(self) -> None:
        pass


sign = Sign(Recorder(), model=models.ALPHA_4120C)
sign.show("Hi")
print(b"".join(sign.transport.sent))
```

`write` must return only once the bytes have left, so that a `pause` after it is
real silence on the line. `read(timeout)` waits up to `timeout` seconds for the
first byte and returns `b""` if none comes; `read(0)` returns only what has already
arrived.

## Write a Command

A Command the library lacks is a small subclass: set the one-character Command
Code, or the Special Function label, and return the data.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar

from alpha_led_sign.protocol import SpecialFunction


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SetSomething(SpecialFunction):
    label: ClassVar[str] = "X"     # the Special Function label from the manual
    value: int

    def encode_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return f"{self.value:02X}".encode("ascii")


sign.send(SetSomething(5))
```

To make validation see what the Command needs, override `codes()` to list the
Modes and Control Codes in its data, or `requirements()` to add other needs. Set
`min_version` when it needs a later Protocol Version, and `must_be_last` when it
must end a Packet.

To decode Responses yourself, `ResponseReader` splits bytes into Responses as they
arrive, and `decode_response` decodes one whole Response Packet.
